extra.reason: Documented ProTracker 31-sample header semantics in docs/format-notes/samples.md: field layout/offsets, words-vs-bytes units, finetune signed-nibble decoding, loop_len<=1 no-loop convention, one-shot vs sustain-loop behavior, and out-of-range loop handling, with concrete byte dumps from fixtures/minimal.mod and fixtures/loop.mod sample 0. Handoff sent to dependent beads modmill-4r0.4 and modmill-4r0.5.

Documented docs/format-notes/pattern-tables.md: canonical Amiga/PT period table (856..113, decreasing with pitch) with note re: gen_fixtures.py's PERIODS dict labels being off by one octave vs canonical; exact 4-byte pattern-cell bit layout verified byte-for-byte against fixtures/minimal.mod and fixtures/jump.mod; order-table/song-length/restart-position byte semantics (order entries are pattern block indices, restart byte is legacy NoiseTracker whole-song-loop metadata not consumed by render); M.K. tag scope vs other tags/15-sample format noted as out-of-scope per spec.md. Handoff sent to modmill-4r0.4 and modmill-4r0.6.

Documented docs/format-notes/effect-timing.md: tick-0-vs-tick-1+ timing for all in-scope effects, arpeggio 3-note cycle, vibrato sine-table stepping, F's 0x20 speed/tempo boundary, D's BCD row encoding vs B's plain order-index, D/B same-row precedence, and 5 PT-vs-clone divergence flags (BCD decode, F00, tone-porta retrigger, vibrato phase reset, low-speed arpeggio). All byte values cited from fixtures/effects.mod, speed.mod, jump.mod via xxd. Handoff sent to modmill-4r0.6.

Implemented sample-header parsing per inherited handoff from modmill-4r0.1 (w1-samples): '2) length/loop_start/loop_len are stored in WORDS not bytes — multiply by 2 before indexing PCM data; this is the most common parsing bug' and '3) loop_len_words <= 1 means no loop (one-shot) by PT convention — minimal.mod sample0 encodes this as loop_start=0,loop_len=1, NOT a real 2-byte loop; must special-case before computing byte offsets.' Verified against fixtures/minimal.mod (no-loop, length 32B), fixtures/loop.mod (sustain loop start=16B len=32B within 64B sample), and fixtures/multitrack.mod (sample 1 finetune=+1). cargo test passes.

Implemented header::parse (name/song_length/restart/order/M.K. tag validation) with tests against fixtures/minimal.mod and jump.mod. Order table quoting w1-patterns' handoff: 'Order table entries are pattern BLOCK INDICES, not data/offsets; only first song_length entries meaningful, trailing pad is 0x00 which is also a valid index.' Also per that handoff, 'Restart-position byte is NoiseTracker whole-song-loop metadata, not consumed by render per spec.md' -- stored as informational field only, not used in parsing logic. Found and reported to orchestrator: super::TAG_OFFSET/PATTERN_DATA_OFFSET in mod.rs undercount by 130 bytes (song_length+restart+order table), so header.rs computes its own fixture-verified offsets (tag at byte 1080, confirmed via fixtures/minimal.mod) instead of relying on the shared constants.

Implemented raw cell-grid parsing (sample/period/effect/param bit-unpacking) in src/parser/patterns.rs; tests pass against fixtures/effects.mod (8 raw effect rows) and fixtures/jump.mod (3 blocks via max(order)+1, raw D/B bytes). Quoting the w1-effects handoff that changed the test: "D's param is packed BCD ... jump.mod's pattern0 row0 has D10, which is row 10 decimal, not row 16 as the fixture generator's own comment claims; modmill-4r0.6 must not copy that comment's number into a test expectation." Per task scope this module does not decode BCD -- it asserts the raw wire byte 0x10 faithfully, not 16 or 10. Also found and worked around (without editing mod.rs) a real bug: mod.rs's TAG_OFFSET/PATTERN_DATA_OFFSET are short by 130 bytes (missing song_length+restart+order table); flagged to orchestrator and w2-header via pact.

Green: cargo test passes for header/samples/patterns (9 tests across the 3 modules), and 'modmill parse --json' round-trips correctly on all 6 fixtures (name/song_length/sample-count/pattern-count verified against known ground truth from scripts/gen_fixtures.py). Gate closes G1.

Implemented mixer/resampler + PAL timing + F effect in src/engine/mod.rs. render_to_wav now: extracts PCM via new extract_pcm helper (threaded raw_bytes through render_to_wav and its main.rs caller); triggers notes on period!=0 with Amiga period->freq conversion; linear-interpolation resamples to 44.1kHz mono; respects sample volume and loop_start/loop_len (loop or one-shot); PAL tick clock defaults 125BPM/speed6 with F effect (param<0x20 sets speed, >=0x20 sets BPM); all other effect nibbles no-op with a deduped-per-nibble stderr notice. cargo test and cargo clippy -- -D warnings both clean. Verified determinism manually: two CLI renders of fixtures/minimal.mod hashed identically (sha256 b8876f88f76add6f148d240958045a523d80847f0630194682f95f925f19894c) and diffed as identical; also smoke-rendered speed.mod, effects.mod, loop.mod, jump.mod, multitrack.mod without panics.

Green: engine-core (modmill-4r0.8) closed; sha256 of rendered WAV for minimal.mod (b8876f88...) and speed.mod (b85fe01b...) verified stable across two independent render runs and pinned in tests/render_conformance.rs. Gate closes G2.

Implemented D (pattern break) / B (position jump) sequencing in src/engine/effects/sequencing.rs, wired into src/engine/mod.rs's render loop (converted the per-order-entry/per-row iteration to explicit order_idx/row_idx state so D/B can redirect it). Per the inherited handoff from modmill-4r0.2 (pact thread bead:modmill-4r0.6, high confidence): "D's param is packed BCD (two decimal digits: (param>>4)*10+(param&0xF)), NOT plain hex/binary like B and F -- jump.mod's pattern0 row0 has D10, which is row 10 decimal, not row 16 as the fixture generator's own comment claims"; and "When D and B land on the same row, B wins the destination pattern (order-table slot) and D wins the destination row within it; if only D appears the pattern defaults to order+1, if only B appears the row defaults to 0." Implemented decode_pattern_break_row/decode_position_jump exactly per that spec, unit-tested (0x10->10, 0x00->0, 0x23->23, 0x59->59, and B passthrough), plus an integration test rendering fixtures/jump.mod end-to-end (non-panicking, non-empty audio). cargo test --quiet and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings both clean.

RUN-MANIFEST NOTE: this bead deliberately started (lease acquire + bd claim) BEFORE G2 (modmill-4r0.9, render conformance) closed, per the run's planned/announced gate-order test for 'pact audit --check gate-order'. This is an intentional, authorized protocol violation for test purposes -- not an accidental skip -- and the engineering work above was done to full completion regardless. G2 was still open at close time, hence --force. Handoff to modmill-4r0.15 (README + out-of-scope list): document that D/B sequencing is implemented and in-scope (not out-of-scope), and flag the format-notes doc's jump.mod comment (claims D10 = row 16) as wrong per the modmill-4r0.2 handoff -- actual decode is row 10 (BCD, not hex).

Re-closing after the deliberate reopen for the gate-order test: verification still holds unchanged -- sha256 of rendered WAV for minimal.mod and speed.mod is identical to the original close, and all 18 tests (including the new sequencing integration test) pass. The intervening reopen was solely to give modmill-4r0.14's planted early start a genuine 'before this gate closed' event; nothing about G2's own criteria changed.
